newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen supported near 115 yen in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen supported near 115 yen in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is expected to be supported near 115 yen during Asian trading time on Thursday with bids from Japanese operators who had failed to buy enough dollars previously, dealers said. It fell below 116 yen overnight.
The market is keeping a close watch on the release of Japan's April industrial production data due out at 0430 GMT and on moves in Japanese market interest rates.
Dealers said stronger-than-expected data and a rise in interest rates would be expected to keep the yen well-bid against the dollar.
"After the dollar fell sharply overnight, operators may be eager to buy dollars on dips," a city bank dealer said.
A trust bank dealer said Japanese investors may kick in to purchase the greenback near 115.00 yen, keeping the dollar's downside solid around that level.
He added the dollar edged down while setting off stop-loss sales near 116 yen and then 115.80 yen overnight.
On the topside, dealers said substantial offers from exporters are not expected near 116 yen, even though they were said to be keen to sell dollars near 117 yen in the past few days.

In New York, the dollar weakened against the mark in a volatile session after mark purchases on rumours that a private poll showed the French Socialists could win a clear majority in the final round of parliamentary elections on Sunday.
The Socialists favour a less stringent interpretation of the criteria that countries must meet in order to qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
But dealers were unsure about the mark's future direction.
"It is still hard to evaluate the EMU issue in Asia," the city bank dealer said.
Dealers said stronger-than-expected data on Japan's industrial production, showing the strength of the Japanese economy, could prompt yen buying for the dollar.
A possible further rise in Japanese market interest rates could also help keep the Japanese currency well-bid, they added.
